statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: Upon the discharge and dismissal of a person pursuant to SDCL § 23A-27-14, a court shall order that all official records, other than the nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation, be sealed along with all records relating to the arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, and dismissal and discharge. The order restores the person to the status occupied before arrest, indictment or information, and the person is not guilty of perjury or of giving a false statement for failing to recite or acknowledge the matter. Sealing is the court's mandatory duty; there is no ordinary participant motion that triggers the initial sealing. The decided product for the recorded failure branch is: expected sealing at discharge and dismissal, verify court access status, a written implementation request in the original case attaching the discharge and dismissal order and asking the clerk or sentencing judge to enter and implement the statutorily required sealing order, a motion in the original criminal docket to enforce § 23A-27-17 if not corrected, and attorney handoff for refusal or mandamus.
doNotImport: Do not use a form designed for the separate arrest-expungement statute as a fallback; the decision forbids it.
Do not ask for sealing before the discharge and dismissal has issued; the statute does not yet direct it.
Do not draft the sealing order itself; the statute makes it the court's order to enter.

Do not say sealing removes every government record for every purpose; the nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation are expressly outside the order and remain available to law enforcement, prosecutors and courts for future sentencing, future SIS eligibility and habitual-offender determinations.
Do not invent a filing fee, a delivery method or a copy count; no committed record this family binds establishes any of them.
Do not decide whether the case was eligible for the suspended imposition of sentence in the first place; an eligibility dispute is a recorded attorney handoff.

Do not tell a certified-teacher licence holder or applicant convicted under the specified subdivisions of § 22-22-1 or under § 22-22-7 that the seal protects the licence; the licensure authority may refuse or revoke notwithstanding §§ 23A-27-14 and 23A-27-17.

documents.title: Filing Instructions

sections.heading: What this packet is for
sections.body: This packet is prepared for asking the original South Dakota court to enter and implement the mandatory SDCL § 23A-27-17 sealing order it did not enter after your discharge and dismissal.

sections.heading: THE ONE SITUATION THIS PACKET IS FOR
sections.body: After a suspended imposition of sentence, when you complete the court's conditions and the court enters the discharge and dismissal, SDCL Sec. 23A-27-17 makes sealing the COURT'S duty: upon the discharge and dismissal a court shall order the official records sealed, other than the nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation. You apply for nothing to obtain it. This packet is only for the case where the discharge and dismissal issued and the sealing did not happen.

sections.heading: WHAT YOU DO, IN ORDER
sections.body:
STEP ONE. Confirm the duty was triggered: your conditions are complete and the order of discharge and dismissal issued. If it has not issued, stop - nothing here applies yet.
STEP TWO. Get the SIS order and the order of discharge and dismissal from the office of the court in the original criminal case, and keep dated evidence of the public record entry that still shows the matter.
STEP THREE. Complete and file the WRITTEN REQUEST in the original case, attaching a copy of the discharge and dismissal order. Ask the office of that court how it accepts delivery and whether any fee applies - no committed record this packet is built from states either.
STEP FOUR. Only if the record is not corrected, complete and file the ENFORCEMENT MOTION in the original criminal docket.
STEP FIVE. Sign and date each page yourself.

sections.heading: WHAT SEALING DOES, AND DOES NOT DO
sections.body: The recorded effect: the order restores you to the status you occupied before arrest, indictment or information, and you are not guilty of perjury or of giving a false statement for failing to recite or acknowledge the matter. The recorded limits: the nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation are expressly outside the sealing order, and sealing is not expungement. If your underlying conviction was under SDCL Sec. 22-22-1 or Sec. 22-22-7 and you hold or seek a certified teaching licence, the recorded caveat is that the licensure authority may refuse or revoke notwithstanding the sealing - get advice before relying on the seal.

sections.heading: WHAT THIS PACKET MUST NEVER BE USED FOR
sections.body:
- As an arrest-expungement filing. The recorded rule: do not use a form designed for a separate arrest-expungement statute as a fallback.
- After a refusal, or where eligibility is disputed. The recorded escalation is attorney handoff for refusal or mandamus.

sections.heading: WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP INSTEAD OF FILING
WHAT THIS PACKET IS NOT
sections.body: This is a prepared set of composed enforcement instruments for one recorded failure branch. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the court will act. Sealing restricts access; it does not erase the DCI's nonpublic records.
